subfamily: Sling as a sparkling sour: the Singapore (Straits) Sling in its 1913 order, one each of cherry brandy, Bénédictine, gin and lime juice, ice, water and bitters (Imbibe! pdf 122; Oxford SINGAPORE SLING pdf 1803); the Codex keeps soda-lengthened sours in its Daiquiri chapter (p. 138)
glass: large rocks glass (about 400 ml), one large ice cube
_status: v1 (Tomás, round 4). The 1913 order as the Singapore Cricket Club's younger members wrote it down, one each of cherry brandy, Bénédictine, gin and lime juice, with ice, water and bitters (Imbibe! pdf 122; Oxford pdf 1803), at Wondrich's 1 oz measure. Built over one large cube with a stir (25% dilution: the collins style's estimate; Arnold gives 24% for a drink built on a rock). Soda 90 ml is mine: Wondrich's 1-2 oz reads OUT with a 47% gin (60 ml: 15.9%). Sweeps: gin 40-47% x soda 75-90 all in range except 47%/75 (15.0-15.1, top of band); lime 25-35, Benedictine 25-35, Heering 25-35 ml in range; cherry liqueur 16-30% and 20-30 g sugar in range, 35 g edge. Rejected: Wondrich's suggested tweak 45/30/15/22.5 (sugar 5.0-5.75 OUT/edge, strength OUT below 90 ml soda); Oxford's 1910s 45/15/15/15 (17.8% and 4.44 g OUT at 60 ml soda; 3.79 g and 0.44% acid OUT at 90). Contains nuts (Cherry Heering, safe-side call). No garnish (Wondrich: 'If you must garnish').
